D: A martial artist goes undercover at a deadly tournament on a crime lord's private island.
P: Serve the mains when Han's island banquet begins.
S: the junk boats sailing out of Hong Kong harbour
Prawn and pork siu mai: mince, chopped prawn, ginger, shiitake and soy wrapped in open wonton skins, steamed 8 minutes. Chilli oil.
the fighters gathering on the island
Cabbage, carrot, mushroom and glass noodles rolled tight in pastry, fried at 180C until golden, with sweet chilli sauce.

Scored squid dusted in rice flour and Sichuan salt and pepper, fried hard and fast, tossed with fried garlic, chilli and spring onion, with lemon. Cut 600g cleaned squid tubes open, score the inside in a crisscross and cut into strips. Toast 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, grind with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp white pepper and mix with 100g rice flour. Toss the squid in the flour and fry in 190C oil for 60 seconds until just crisp. Stir-fry 3 sliced garlic cloves, a sliced red chilli and 2 spring onions for 30 seconds, toss with the squid and serve with lemon.
M: the lavish feast on Han's island

Duck legs salted overnight, rubbed with five-spice and roasted until the skin crackles, shredded into steamed pancakes with cucumber, spring onion and hoisin. Rub 4 duck legs with 2 tsp salt and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight. Rub with 2 tsp five spice and roast skin up on a rack at 180C for 90 minutes, then 10 minutes at 220C until crisp. Shred the meat and skin with two forks. Steam 20 Chinese pancakes for 3 minutes. Serve with batons of a cucumber, shredded spring onion and a bowl of hoisin sauce.
Pork neck marinated overnight in hoisin, soy, honey, five-spice and Shaoxing wine, roasted at 200C and glazed, sliced over egg fried rice.
W: a Hong Kong dessert shop favourite
Thin crêpes of flour, egg, milk and sugar cooked in a non-stick pan, cooled, wrapped around whipped cream and a thick slice of fresh mango, folded into neat parcels and chilled an hour.
K: Iced chrysanthemum and goji honey tea

Dried chrysanthemum flowers and goji berries steeped with rock sugar and honey, chilled and poured over ice with a squeeze of lemon. Bring 1.2L water to the boil, take off the heat and add 15g dried chrysanthemum flowers, 2 tbsp goji berries and 50g rock sugar. Steep for 6 minutes, stirring until the sugar melts, then strain, keeping the goji berries. Stir in 1 tbsp honey and cool, then chill for an hour. Pour over ice in four glasses, drop in a few goji berries and add a squeeze of lemon.

s.note: the junk boats sailing out of Hong Kong harbour
s.how: Mix 300g pork mince, 150g chopped prawns, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 50g chopped shiitake and soy. Spoon into 24 wonton wrappers, pinch up the sides and steam 8 minutes. Serve with chilli oil.

s.note: the fighters gathering on the island
s.how: Stir-fry 2 cups shredded wombok, a grated carrot and 100g sliced shiitake. Add 50g soaked glass noodles and soy, then cool. Roll tight in 16 spring roll wrappers and fry at 180C until golden. Serve with sweet chilli.

m.how: Marinate 800g pork neck overnight in 4 tbsp hoisin, 2 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tsp five spice and 2 tbsp Shaoxing. Roast at 200C for 35 minutes, glazing twice. Fry 300g cooked jasmine rice with 2 eggs and spring onion. Slice the pork over.

w.note: a Hong Kong dessert shop favourite
w.how: Whisk 120g flour, 2 eggs, 300ml milk and 2 tbsp sugar and rest. Cook 8 thin crêpes in a non-stick pan and cool. Wrap each around whipped cream from 300ml and a thick slice of mango from 2 mangoes. Fold into parcels and chill an hour.
